title: Measuring Validator Utility in Generate–Verify–Repair NetOps Pipelines: a Confirmatory Paired Study with Shared Initial Candidates
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study (AC-2026-03) to evaluate whether a multidimensional validator metric suite predicts end-to-end agentic NetOps success better than a single verifier pass rate. Using a synthetic intent→configuration generator and a hosted generate–validate–repair (GVR) adapter under shared_initial_candidate semantics, we ran 200 paired tasks (one shared initial generation per task reused for baseline and guarded). The deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) judged every sampled initial candidate valid; no repairs were applied. Baseline = 200/200, guarded = 200/200, paired difference = 0.00 (bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.00], exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; bootstrap_seed=1729, resamples=10000). The observed ceiling invalidated the preregistered power assumptions (targeted 10 percentage-point paired improvement) and rendered the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. We report preregistered design choices, full execution accounting, exact analysis results, an exemplar validator-trace excerpt, and an evidence-grounded interpretation of why the run could not estimate validator-driven repair utility. We conclude with concrete, artifact-grounded next-step preregistered experiment prescriptions (fault injection, multi-sample stochastic generation, multi-validator comparison) required to measure validator coverage and repair value.

sections.introduction: LLMs and agentic workflows are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into executable network configurations and to automate NetOps maintenance workflows. Practical deployments typically interpose deterministic validators and repair loops in generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipelines as a safety pattern: generators propose candidate actions, validators mechanically check correctness and policy constraints, and repair layers may produce corrected candidates before acceptance. Despite prior demonstrations of GVR-style patterns in code and system settings [1], rigorous, preregistered measurements of validator coverage (FP/FN rates), detection latency, and predictive value for end-to-end guarded success in NetOps are limited. To address that measurement gap we preregistered study AC-2026-03 with a confirmatory paired design that isolates downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The study tested the primary hypothesis (H1) that a multidimensional validator-metric suite explains more variance in end-to-end task success than a single verifier pass rate; primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Our contributions are (1) a preregistered, machine-readable paired experiment that isolates validator/repair effects via shared_initial_candidate semantics; (2) a closed execution with full accounting and archived artifacts; (3) transparent reporting of a degenerate (ceiling) confirmatory outcome and its statistical implications; and (4) concrete artifact-grounded prescriptions for next-step preregistered experiments needed to estimate validator utility.
sections.related_work: Prior work motivates validator layers and GVR-style architectures to detect mechanically verifiable defects and to provide structured repair feedback to generative systems [1]. Controlled NetOps/AIOps benchmark suites document substantial failure modes—ticket noise, false-premise reports, and wrong-but-plausible outputs—that complicate end-to-end automation and motivate verifier insertion [2],[3]. Recent system reports and prototypes advocate self-healing orchestrators, auditable decision traces, and verifier-guided repair to reduce silent or action-triggering failures in tool-augmented LLM systems [4]. Survey literature on LLMs for telecommunications and NetOps contextualizes adaptation and verification trade-offs and motivates metricized evaluation of verification cost versus nominal correctness [5]. These references motivate our measurement focus but do not provide a standardized validator-metric suite for NetOps GVR flows; our preregistered study was designed to begin addressing that measurement gap under strict preregistration.
sections.methodology: Design and preregistration. The confirmatory paired design and analysis plan were preregistered (study_id AC-2026-03). Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Declared model: gpt-5-mini via provider bundle 'openai_responses' (execution manifest records declared_model_version="gpt-5-mini"). Task bank: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 produced intent_configuration_repair_v1 tasks at difficulty levels 'very_hard' and 'extreme' with explicit allowed-field and required-sequence constraints. Key preregistered execution semantics: task_count = 200 pairs (planned_episode_count=400), generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate, initial_generation_calls_per_task = 1, maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. The preregistration explicitly recorded that independent_condition_generation = false; therefore baseline and guarded used the identical initial sampled candidate per pair and any paired outcome difference could only arise from downstream validator-triggered repair or deterministic pipeline steps. Model configuration and sampling note (artifact-grounded): execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature=0. The adapter used exactly one shared initial generation per task (execution_manifest.stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200) and thus model_calls_used = 200 (one call per pair) whereas maximum_model_calls prerregistered = 400. Task selection and contamination controls. The sampling plan used deterministic task indices from the preregistered challenging_workflow_stress_v1 generator; contamination rules and exclusion criteria were preregistered (duplicate SHA-256 exclusions, semantic-similarity exclusions with embedding threshold >0.95). Recorded execution artifacts show no contamination exclusions (analysis/contamination_summary.csv empty) and no exclusions in the final analysis. Validator and scoring. Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0). The validator performed a mechanistic intent-constraint check producing: normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_count/violation_codes, valid (boolean), repair_applied (boolean), and validator trace fields for before/after validation. Scoring rule for the primary confirmatory outcome was the preregistered binary validity label (full_intent_constraint_validation). Statistical analysis plan. Primary confirmatory test: paired binary analysis (exact two-sided McNemar), with paired bootstrap percentile confidence intervals (bootstrap_resamples = 10000, bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered power calculation targeted detection of an absolute paired improvement of 0.10 (10 percentage points) with alpha = 0.05 and ~80% power under conservative baseline assumptions (baseline p explored across 0.3–0.7). Missingness and retry policy. Preregistered missingness rules and retry policy: maximum_attempts_per_call = 1 (no manual retries); incomplete pairs would be handled by planned sensitivity analyses; actual execution recorded completed_episode_count = 400 and failed_episode_count = 0.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and artifact summary. The adapter-complete execution followed the preregistered contract: planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair), maximum_model_calls = 400. Provider-call audit (deterministic_reconciliation.provider_call_audit): hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 200. Contamination and missingness summaries are empty (analysis/contamination_summary.csv and analysis/missingness_summary.csv show zeros), and no preregistered exclusion rules were triggered. Confirmatory primary outcome. The deterministic validator judged every shared initial candidate valid and required no repairs. Summary counts: complete_pair_count = 200, baseline_success_count = 200, guarded_success_count = 200. Paired contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n_11 = 200, n_10 = 0, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.00. Exact McNemar two-sided test: p = 1.0. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729): [0.00, 0.00]. Validator/repair traces. For every episode validator_trace.validation_after.valid = true and validator_trace.repair_applied = false. Representative validator-trace excerpt (artifact: execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json) compressed to key fields:  
  - pair_id: pair-000004
  - normalized_configuration: "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down"
  - parsed_command_count: 4
  - required_command_count: 4
  - valid: true
  - repair_applied: false
This exemplar illustrates the deterministic intent-constraint checks the validator enforces: parsed/required command counts matched and no violation codes were emitted, so no repair prompt was issued. Consequence for inference. The observed ceiling (baseline success rate = 1.0) violates the preregistered power assumptions (which presumed a non-degenerate baseline near p≈0.5). Under complete ceiling the paired test is uninformative for the preregistered 10-percentage-point improvement target: there is no observable room for validator-triggered repair to increase final validity because the initial candidates already satisfied the validator's mechanistic checks. Secondary and exploratory metrics. Per-validator FP/FN/latency distributions are degenerate in this execution (no observed false positives or false negatives; detection-latency distributions uninformative). The analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) and the full raw_results.jsonl and validator traces are archived in the execution bundle for reanalysis.
sections.discussion:
Design interpretation under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Because preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate and independent_condition_generation = false, both baseline (single-shot validity) and guarded (final validity after permitted repair) evaluated the identical sampled initial candidate for each pair. Thus any paired difference could only arise from deterministic validator-triggered repair (or other deterministic pipeline repairs), not from independent generator sampling differences. This choice isolates validator/repair utility but also concentrates risk of a ceiling if the generator's sampled seeds produce valid-by-validator candidates at high frequency. Causes of the ceiling outcome. The execution-level evidence suggests three determinants for the observed ceiling: (1) task/fault prevalence in the synthetic bank—these generated tasks, despite being labeled 'very_hard'/'extreme', produced candidates that satisfied the validator's mechanistic constraints for the recorded model seeds; (2) generator sampling regime (single shared sample per task) left no opportunity to observe generator variability across draws; and (3) validator coverage: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee identification of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent). Practical implications and next-step preregistered experiment prescriptions. The archived artifacts permit us to derive artifact-grounded prescriptions for follow-up confirmatory designs that would allow estimation of validator FP/FN behavior and repair utility:  
  - Fault-injection arm (preregistered): inject a controlled fraction f of targeted faults (syntactic errors, configuration-logic faults, and semantic intent mismatches) into reference answers so baseline validity < 1.0 while maintaining reproducible seed control. The execution bundle already supports deterministic task replacement rules and contamination checks required for this arm.  
  - Multi-sample stochastic generation: change initial_generation_calls_per_task to k ≥ 3 independent draws per task (with independent sampling seeds recorded) and adapt the estimand to allow guarded acceptance of any validator-approved candidate among the k draws; this will permit measurement of generator variability and of repair benefit when the validator rejects some draws.  
  - Multi-validator comparison: include at least one alternative validator implementation and at least two model families to probe external validity and validator-coverage sensitivity.  
Each of these steps is prespecified in the evidence-grounded recommendations in the manuscript_evidence_bundle and is feasible within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter semantics. Reproducibility and artifact pointers. All preregistration records, execution manifests, raw model responses, per-episode validator traces, analysis artifacts (paired contingency table, bootstrap parameters, analysis_log.jsonl), and model_configuration.json (temperature = null/unset) are archived in the execution bundle (execution/execution_manifest.json and referenced artifact paths). Researchers may inspect: execution/raw_results.jsonl, execution/task_manifest.jsonl, execution/model_configuration.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and representative episode scorer artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000004-guarded.json) to validate every reported value. Limitations and threats to validity. The single-model, synthetic-bank execution limits external validity: the synthetic tasks are not equivalent to heterogeneous production topologies and human ticket noise; the deterministic validator enforces mechanistic checks but cannot be assumed to detect semantic intent misalignment; and shared_initial_candidate semantics intentionally isolate validator/repair effects at the cost of producing a single-sample ceiling vulnerability. These limitations are explicit and supported by the archived artifacts and analysis results; they motivate the preregistered next-step designs above.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory study under shared_initial_candidate semantics to measure validator utility in NetOps GVR flows. For the synthetic task bank, gpt-5-mini sampled seeds, and the deterministic validator used here, every sampled initial candidate satisfied the validator's mechanistic intent-constraint checks so no repairs were applied and guarded success equaled baseline (200/200). The preregistered power assumptions (targeting a 10 percentage‑point improvement from a non-degenerate baseline) were invalidated by the observed ceiling, rendering the primary confirmatory test uninformative for the originally planned effect. This degenerate but transparently archived outcome emphasizes that robust measurement of validator coverage and repair utility requires preregistered designs that introduce measurable fault prevalence (fault injection), measure generator variability (multi-sample draws), and include multiple validators and model families. We provide exact execution and analysis artifacts to support replication and to guide preregistered follow-ups that can estimate validator FP/FN behavior and repair value in operationally meaningful conditions.

limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics constrained inference: baseline and guarded reused the same initial candidate; any paired difference could only arise from validator-triggered repair (not independent generator sampling).
Synthetic task bank (difficulty 'very_hard'/'extreme') is not equivalent to heterogeneous production networks (multi-vendor devices, real ticket noise); external validity is limited.
Single-model experiment: only gpt-5-mini was executed; no multi-model generality claims are made.

No repairs were applied because all initial candidates passed the deterministic validator; therefore the study could not estimate repair effectiveness or validator false-negative behavior in this execution.

Validator scope: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces mechanistic intent-constraint checks but does not guarantee detection of semantic intent misalignment (correct-by-structure but incorrect-by-intent).
Recorded execution/model_configuration.json temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling; provider-side sampling behavior may vary and is documented in execution manifests.
